title: Accelerating Personalized PageRank Vector Computation

problem.claim: Efficiently calculating Personalized PageRank Vectors for directed and undirected graphs.

gap.claim: At high precision, FwdPush has runtime similar to power iteration and is bounded by O(m over α log 1 over ε), motivating improved acceleration methods and tighter convergence analysis.

contributions.claim: Introduces FwdPushSOR, a Successive Over-Relaxation-based modification of FwdPush for accelerating PPV computation, and characterizes FwdPush as a variant of Gauss-Seidel using a linear invariant property.
Proves a local linear convergence rate for FwdPush of O(vol (S) over α log 1 over ε).
Designs a local heuristic push method for reducing operations and two momentum-based acceleration methods for undirected graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on six real-world graph datasets report efficiency for FwdPushSOR on directed graphs and for the acceleration methods on undirected graphs.
The local heuristic push method is reported to reduce the number of operations by 10–50 percent compared to FwdPush.
The momentum-based methods are reported to speed up non-accelerated methods by O(1 / √α) for undirected graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: PPVs are used in graph-learning tasks including spammer detection, graph embedding, and graph neural network training.
FwdPush provides a sublinear approximation rate, but at high precision its runtime can resemble power iteration and has a pessimistic bound.
The paper analyzes PPV computation on directed and undirected graphs, proposes FwdPushSOR, and proves a local linear convergence rate for FwdPush.
It adds a local heuristic push method and momentum-based undirected-graph accelerators, with reported operation reductions, asymptotic speedup, and experiments on six real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Momentum-based methods are expressed as one-line updates and are reported to speed up non-acceleration methods by O(1 / √α) on undirected graphs.

interpretation.claim: Simple update-rule modifications can yield theoretically characterized acceleration in iterative numerical methods.

application.claim: When adapting iterative solvers for undirected graph problems, consider momentum-based updates with explicit dependence on the damping parameter.

exception.claim: The reported speedup is scoped to undirected graphs and the abstract does not establish its behavior on directed graphs.

unknowns: Exact definitions and derivations of the convergence bounds.
Details of the six graph datasets, experimental setup, baselines, and statistical results.
Conditions under which the reported operation reductions and speedups are achieved.
